title: Assessment feedback and reteaching
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: In the assessment, what was the value after the first bubble pass on [6,2,5,1]?
How do you compensate for shifting the mantissa left one place?
options: Reduce the exponent by one.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
This result cannot be obtained using the stated method.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Reduce the exponent by one.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: diagnosis — Identifying the specific cause of an error.
method mark — Credit awarded for a correct intermediate step.
transfer — Apply a method to a different problem.
reteaching — Explain a weak concept again, with better modelling.
correction — A justified replacement for an incorrect answer.

blocks.title: Diagnose by question
blocks.text: A low Q1 mark suggests data structure operations; Q2 suggests algorithm traces and efficiency; Q3 suggests representation or Boolean rules.

blocks.title: Model a precise correction
blocks.text: Correct each lost method step, including the relevant input and why the operation occurs.

blocks.title: Retest with a different input
blocks.text: Do not just memorise the assessment numbers. Transfer the method to a new problem.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: [2,5,6,1] is an intermediate state; the last comparison 6 versus 1 is still outstanding.

blocks.title: Worked example · Check the method
blocks.text: Swap 6 and 1. Correct pass-1 end is [2,5,1,6].

questions.prompt: Choose the response that best addresses this independent task: RETEACH Q1 · 6 MARKS · QUESTION 1 OF 3 Insert 30,15,45,22 into an empty BST. Identify the root, parent of 22 and whether 22 is a left/right child. Explain your comparison path.
questions.answer: [6] Root 30 [1]; 15 is left of 30 [1]; 45 is right of 30 [1]; 22 is greater than 15 [1] but less than 30 [1], so right child of 15 [1].
